findings.title: Crooks Steal Phone, SMS Records for Nearly All AT&T Customers
findings.summary_md: First coverage of the AT&T disclosure: in an SEC filing the same day, AT&T said call and text metadata for roughly 110 million people was accessed in April 2024 from an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform (Snowflake) protected by username and password only, with no MFA. The records covered May 1 to Oct. 31, 2022 and Jan. 2, 2023, and a subset included cell-tower identifiers that could approximate device location. AT&T learned of the breach April 19, 2024 and delayed disclosure at the FBI's request; TechCrunch tied the theft to a breach affecting more than 160 Snowflake customers.

findings.title: Hacker in Snowflake Extortions May Be a U.S. Soldier
findings.summary_md: KrebsOnSecurity reported that Kiberphant0m, the handle selling data stolen from Snowflake customers and publicly extorting AT&T and Verizon, appeared to be a U.S. Army soldier stationed in South Korea, based on chat records reviewed with Flashpoint, Intel 471, and Unit 221B. After co-conspirator Connor Riley Moucka's Oct. 30, 2024 arrest, Kiberphant0m posted claimed AT&T call logs for Donald Trump and Kamala Harris plus an NSA 'data schema', offered Verizon push-to-talk call logs on Nov. 5, and advertised a SIM-swapping service on Nov. 9.

findings.title: U.S. Army Soldier Arrested in AT&T, Verizon Extortions
findings.summary_md: Federal authorities arrested Cameron John Wagenius, 20, near Fort Hood, Texas on Dec. 20, 2024 on a two-count indictment for unlawful transfer of confidential phone records; the case was later transferred to the Western District of Washington. KrebsOnSecurity identified him as Kiberphant0m, a communications specialist recently stationed in South Korea who claimed intrusions into at least 15 telecommunications firms. Unit 221B chief research officer Allison Nixon said the opsec mistake that unmasked him was found Nov. 10 and his last Telegram activity was Dec. 6, 2024.

findings.title: Former U.S. Soldier Pleads Guilty to Hacking and Extortion Scheme Involving Telecommunications Companies
findings.summary_md: DOJ announced Wagenius pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud, extortion in relation to computer fraud, and aggravated identity theft. Court documents say that between April 2023 and Dec. 18, 2024 he used the kiberphant0m nickname to defraud at least 10 victim organizations, obtaining credentials with a tool called SSH Brute and moving them via Telegram, then extorting victims on BreachForums and XSS.is for at least $1 million while on active duty. DOJ credited Flashpoint and Unit 221B with assistance; sentencing was then scheduled for Oct. 6.
